author: ojiudezue
title: Zone-1 strands are REAL Carrier manual holds created after URA's return — the status-lag misread (144) is wrong
summary: The W1-B completeness review showed the source never proves hold_activity is authoritative. The recorder settles it: in all 5 strands hold_activity also reads manual (same second as status in 3/5, within 5 min in 2/5) and stays manual for hours. These are genuine Carrier-side manual holds appearing right after URA's own borrow return, not URA misreading a lagging status.
why: Entry 144 generalised from the first few minutes of each strand (status manual, config still named) to the whole strand; the config feed flips too and the hold persists across Carrier's 2-hour full reconciles, which a pure status lag could not survive.
implications: W1-B keeps presets-only returns (a return must never create a manual hold) and drops the status/config coherence rule; a manual hold that appears right after URA's own write at URA's values is URA-owned by provenance and is reclaimed — never while a borrow is live. Leading cause (UNVERIFIED): the return's raw setpoint write + a discarded/reverted named pin (pin over an anonymous hold is discarded unless resume clears it; ha_carrier's shared post-write guard can be wiped early).
revisit_trigger: W1-A write rows capture preset_mode + hold_activity at write time; if a strand shows config named while status manual for its whole duration, the status-lag mechanism returns.
